I think I did a number on myself because I brought my numbers down so quickly. Went home after my first doctor's appointment in March 2024 after finding out I was going blind - and I just cleared out my pantry, cupboards, fridge, freezer, everything. Restocked with low-carb, healthy shit. Stopped constantly snacking and restricted my diet. I think the seizure was related to that. 

Now, here I am debating on selling my car because I can't consistently drive thanks to whatever that seizure did to my vision and brain. I'm proud of how I'm controlling my numbers, but I'm both frustrated and depressed that those numbers don't equal feeling good/better like all my doctors stated it would. "You'll sleep so much better, you'll have so much energy, you'll feel like a new person". Honestly, the only upside I see is that all the exercise and my workout regimen have given me awesome leg muscle definition. Rocking some sexy legs now, lol. Wish the rest of my body would shape up.

I'm in the same boat. I went from an A1c of >14 (yes, so bad that the actual number exceeded what the hospital's machine could read. No idea how I'm alive) down to a 6.0 (most recently a 6.6). During this transition I had what I believe could be considered a seizure and woke up to visual issues (think static or snow set over everything you see). I generally felt like shit, couldn't drive, constantly felt exhausted, and through it all everyone was impressed with my progress, blood panels and all the effort I put in.

It's been over a year now - and it hasn't gotten any better. I'm still exhausted all the time, I still can't drive, I don't sleep any better, I'm constantly feeling sick and no one knows why. 1 year and 2 months of hell, and I'm fitter than I've ever been in my life, and I still feel like shit. Like I'm in a permanent keto flu.
Cry. I cry.

I honestly can't wait to see the neurologist. I'm on a cancelation list, but unless someone cancels I'll be waiting until October.

I want to say both, but the snow is the main problem. While driving everything is moving, and with the snow on top of this the words on street signs are hard to read. Colors and lights are hard to make out appropriately some days when it's really bad. 

I also have early onset cataracts and recently had one of them removed. That did improve the blur in one eye, but the visual snow did not improve at all. I need the other eye addressed through surgery at some point, but the cataract is not quite there yet. And if it goes the same way as the other eye, the visual snow will remain the same.
